name: Sukiyabashi Jiro, Ginza
why: Where Bourdain said he'd want to die mid-meal: twenty-odd pieces of Edomae sushi from the Ono family, in a basement under a Ginza office block. He sat at the counter in a No Reservations deleted scene and talked about it for years after.
tips: Seats go through hotel concierges or premium booking services, often months out
Far over a backpacker budget; worth knowing about even if you only walk past

name: Sushi Karaku, Ginza
why: A Cook's Tour, 2002: after the dawn tuna auction, Bourdain and a sushi chef came here for the meal that opened his first Japan episode. Edomae sushi in a quiet Ginza basement.
tips: Book ahead through an online reservation service
Lunch sets are the gentler way in

name: Chanko Edosawa, Ryogoku
why: After watching morning practice at a sumo stable, Bourdain sat down to chanko nabe, the big communal hot pot wrestlers bulk up on. Ryogoku is sumo town; this is the classic place to try it.
tips: Pair with the Ryogoku Kokugikan sumo museum next door
Hot pot is sized for two or more; solo, ask for a single portion at lunch

name: Bar Ishinohana, Shibuya
why: No Reservations Tokyo: Bourdain sipped a 'Claudia' cocktail from champion bartender Shinobu Ishigaki. Japanese bartending at its most precise: hand-cut ice, exact pours, quiet room.
tips: Cover charge plus ¥1,800–2,500 per cocktail
Dress a notch up from hostel-casual

name: Piano Bar, Nonbei Yokocho
why: A late-night stop on No Reservations Tokyo: a doll's-house bar in Shibuya's 'Drunkard's Alley', a lantern-lit lane of tiny bars right by the station.
tips: Seats about eight; peek in and smile
Cash; small cover charge
mapsQuery: Piano Bar, Nonbei Yokocho, Shibuya, Tokyo

name: New York Grill, Park Hyatt
localName: ニューヨーク グリル
why: Parts Unknown Tokyo, 2013. The 52nd-floor bar from Lost in Translation, with the whole city lit up below. Bourdain came for the view and the whisky.
tips: The hotel reopened after a long renovation; check hours before going
A drink at the bar costs far less than dinner
mapsQuery: New York Grill, Park Hyatt Tokyo, Shinjuku

name: Atelier Morimoto XEX, Roppongi
why: Iron Chef Morimoto cooked monkfish for Bourdain here on No Reservations. High-end teppan and sushi in Roppongi.
tips: Splurge territory; check it is still open under this name before going
mapsQuery: Atelier Morimoto XEX, Roppongi, Tokyo, Japan

name: Ginza Sushi-ko Honten
why: Parts Unknown 'Japan with Masa', 2016: chef Masa Takayama took Bourdain back to the Ginza counter where he trained as a teenager. Old-school Edomae sushi, family-run since 1885.
tips: Reserve ahead; lunch is easier
Ask for the counter

name: Tsukiji Outer Market
why: Bourdain filmed the old Tsukiji tuna auction in 2002 and again with Naomichi Yasuda in 2013. The wholesale market moved to Toyosu in 2018, but the outer market's 400-odd stalls still do breakfast: tamagoyaki, uni, grilled scallops.
tips: Go early, by 8 am; many stalls close by early afternoon
The tuna auction itself is now at Toyosu (book the viewing deck online)

name: Mahakala, Nakameguro
why: Parts Unknown Tokyo: Bourdain and sushi master Naomichi Yasuda went for kushiage (fried skewers: shrimp and basil, octopus, quail eggs) and okonomiyaki.
tips: Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.
Status unclear; check before going

name: Jiyuken, Namba
why: No Reservations Osaka: 'meibutsu curry', with the rice and curry already mixed and a raw egg cracked on top. Open since 1910, and a favorite of the novelist Sakunosuke Oda. Cheap, fast, an Osaka original.
tips: Stir the egg in, then add a dash of Worcestershire like the regulars do
Expect a short queue at lunch

name: Kani Doraku Dotonbori
localName: かに道楽 道頓堀本店
why: Under the giant moving crab: Bourdain grabbed grilled crab legs from the street cart out front on No Reservations. Peak Dotonbori.
tips: The street cart is the cheap version; the restaurant upstairs is a crab splurge

name: Kuidaore Taro, Dotonbori
why: Not food: the drumming clown mascot of 'eat till you drop' Osaka. Bourdain faced his famous fear of clowns here. Take the photo.
tips: Free; it's a statue by a shop front

name: Fukutaro, Sennichimae
why: The okonomiyaki finale of Bourdain's Osaka night, by most accounts. Savory pancakes and negiyaki griddled in front of you; one of the city's best.
tips: Queue forms at opening; put your name down and wander
Get the negiyaki (green onion) as well as the classic

name: Takonotetsu, Umeda
why: Make-your-own takoyaki: you turn the octopus balls in the griddle yourself. Fans tie it to Bourdain's Osaka takoyaki scene. (The other takoyaki spot, Pizza Ball House, has closed.)
tips: Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.
Fun solo or with a group

name: Gosakudon, Tennoji
why: No Reservations Osaka opened in a sushi sports bar packed with Hanshin Tigers fans screaming at the TV. Fitting for a Japan Series trip; check it still exists, or find the nearest Tigers bar on game night.
tips: Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.
On a Tigers night, any bar with a TV near Tennoji or Namba will do

name: Rokkakudo Temple
why: The birthplace of ikebana. Bourdain took a flower-arranging lesson here on No Reservations. A small, central temple with swans in the pond and a stump said to mark the city's center.
tips: Free to enter the grounds
Five minutes' walk from Karasuma-Oike station

name: Yamanoo, Kanazawa
why: Parts Unknown 'Japan with Masa': formal kaiseki in an old ryotei above the Higashi Chaya teahouse district. Sea bream over rice, rockfish smoked in wormwood, Noto wagyu.
tips: Splurge; book ahead
Lunch kaiseki is cheaper

name: Higashi Chaya District
why: Bourdain had tea with a former geisha at the Fujinoya teahouse in this preserved 1820s quarter of wooden teahouses. Walk it at dusk when the lamps come on.
tips: Some teahouses open to the public (Shima, Kaikaro)
Gold-leaf soft serve is the local gimmick, and it's fun

name: Nanao Fish Market (Fisherman’s Wharf)
why: No Reservations 'Cook It Raw' (2011): after a morning at sea, Bourdain ate a fisherman's breakfast in the market restaurant. Noto was hit hard by the 2024 earthquake, so check what has reopened.
tips: Verify opening status (Noto quake recovery)
Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.

name: Tsukimura, Nasushiobara
why: Chef Masa Takayama's brother Kazuo has run this sushi counter in Masa's hometown for over 30 years. Parts Unknown 'Japan with Masa' came here. Way off the tourist track.
tips: Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.
Call ahead; small family restaurant

name: Sapporo Beer Garden (jingisukan)
why: No Reservations Hokkaido opened here: jingisukan, lamb grilled on a dome-shaped skillet at the table, washed down with beer brewed on site in an 1890 brick hall.
tips: All-you-can-eat-and-drink sets are the move
Wear clothes you don't mind smelling of lamb

name: Yakitori Torimatsu, Kutchan
why: Bourdain ate yakitori with Japanese snowboarders at an izakaya in Kutchan, the town at the foot of Niseko. Locals identify it as Torimatsu.
tips: Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.
Kutchan is the train stop for Niseko

name: Makishi Public Market, Naha
why: Parts Unknown Okinawa: buy fish downstairs (parrotfish, sea grapes, gurukun) and the restaurants upstairs cook it for a small fee. Bourdain ate sashimi and fried porcupine fish here.
tips: The market was rebuilt in 2023, same idea
Upstairs cooking fee is a few hundred yen per dish
mapsQuery: Makishi Public Market, Naha, Naha, Japan

name: Urizun, Naha
why: Old Okinawan izakaya where Bourdain tried tofuyo (fermented tofu, eaten in tiny nibbles) and awamori. Classic island food.
tips: Order the dururu-ten (taro croquettes)
Awamori comes neat or with water

name: King Tacos, Kin
localName: キングタコス 金武本店
why: Birthplace of taco rice, the Okinawa-meets-US-base mash-up Bourdain ate on Parts Unknown. Taco filling, cheese, lettuce, salsa on rice. Cheap and enormous.
tips: Original shop is by Camp Hansen in Kin
Cash; the regular size feeds one very hungry person

name: Dojo Bar, Naha
why: Karate-themed bar where Bourdain drank habushu, awamori with a pit viper coiled in the bottle. Run by a martial artist who appears in the episode.
tips: Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.
Habushu tastes better than it looks

name: Sekiyou Ryokan, Yugawara
why: A Cook's Tour 'Dining with Geishas': Bourdain's first proper ryokan, kaiseki dinner and hot spring, an hour from Tokyo near Atami. Splurge-level.
tips: Pin is approximate; Directions searches the name.
Day-trip onsen in Yugawara town are the budget alternative
